misconceptions.description: Assuming all visible color comes from chemical pigment
misconceptions.trigger: learner explains Morpho coloration only through dye chemistry
misconceptions.feedback: Many biological colors are structural. Their appearance depends on geometry, interference, scattering, and wavelength-selective reflection.

misconceptions.description: Copying the visible hue instead of the optical architecture
misconceptions.trigger: learner proposes matching only the final color without discussing microstructure
misconceptions.feedback: The biomimetic principle is in the light-manipulating structure. Matching the visual color alone misses the mechanism.

misconceptions.description: Assuming finer nanostructures always improve optical performance
misconceptions.trigger: learner treats smaller scale as automatically optimal
misconceptions.feedback: Optical performance depends on how feature size relates to wavelength and viewing conditions. The best scale depends on the design goal.
